title: Variables and values
excerpt: A variable gives a value a name. Assignment updates which value that name refers to.
body: Use `let` when the binding will change and `const` when it will not be reassigned. In `score = score + 1`, the right side is evaluated first, then the result is stored back in score.

title: Making decisions with conditions
excerpt: An if statement runs its block only when its boolean condition is true.
body: Comparisons such as `count > 0` produce a boolean. An `else` branch handles the case where the condition is false. Check boundary values such as zero to catch off-by-one mistakes.

title: Loops and iteration
excerpt: A loop repeats a block while its continuation condition allows another iteration.
body: For a counted loop, check the initial value, stopping condition, and update step. A loop with `i < 4` and `i` starting at zero visits 0, 1, 2, and 3.

title: Arrays and collections
excerpt: Arrays store ordered values, and JavaScript array indexes start at zero.
body: An array with length 3 has valid indexes 0, 1, and 2. Use the length property to reason about bounds, and remember that reading beyond the final index does not return another element.

title: Functions and reusable behavior
excerpt: A function can take inputs through parameters and send a result back with return.
body: Calling a function runs its body. `return` gives the caller a value and ends that function call. A parameter is the name in the definition; an argument is the value passed at a call site.
